text:
Sanjay: quick question — we still undecided on scrub/sampling split for telemetry. we're seeing a lot of high-cardinality from prompt_hash, user_id, request_id in spans. do we prefer exporter-side scrubbing (SDK/agent), ingest-side (collector), or a hybrid? @eng-platform

Claire: lean ingest-side for centralized rules. exporters get out of date and apps don't always upgrade. ingest means we can change regexes/whitelists without pushing apps. :thinking:

Alex: agreed on central control but exporter-side has strong benefits: drop payload size early, deterministic bucketing with tenant salt, and faster backpressure. tradeoff is loss of raw for reprocessing unless we keep a short raw window.

Maya: dashboards blow up when request_id or full prompts leak. yesterday a panel exploded because a span.attr.service_request had a full UUID. can we use prefix-bucketing instead of full strings? e.g., store first 8 chars of a salted hash so top-n still works.

Claire: proposal: tag attributes that are "high_cardinality" and for those store only an 8-char salted hex + bucket id (0-99). keep a boolean "raw_kept" when we keep raw for a short TTL for debugging. that gives both observability and cardinality control.

Sanjay: prototype idea — exporter computes prompt_hash = sha256(prompt + salt) and emits prompt_bucket = int(hex(prefix),16) % 100 and prompt_hash8 = prefix[:8]. then collector verifies bucket if salt rotation happened.

Alex: example OTLP exporter config (SDK-level helper):

```yaml\notel:
  attributes:
    - key: "prompt"
      action: "hash_and_bucket"
      salt_source: "tenant_id"
      keep_chars: 8
      buckets: 100
    - key: "user.id"
      action: "anonymize_prefix"
      keep_chars: 4
```

Maya: ingest-team suggests raw spans TTL = 48h, then roll to aggregated metric rows for long term. this keeps SLO debugging windows but prevents long-term cardinality noise. cc @eng-sre and Grafana owners.

ingest-bot: retention policy draft applied to dev cluster: raw_spans: 48h, rolled_metrics: 365d. docs: https://go/internal/telemetry/policies (dev only)

Sanjay: next steps: Claire to draft collector scrub pipeline PR with tests; Alex to add exporter helpers to JS/Python SDKs; Maya to add dashboard query guards and grafana alerts for cardinality spikes. we'll reconvene Tue. Ping if blockers.

Claire: on it — will include deterministic salt rotation plan and a migration strategy for existing prompt_hash fields.

Alex: I'll mock SDK helpers and a tiny CLI tool to compute buckets so infra can validate.

Maya: I'll also create a quick runbook for oncall: how to identify a leak and enable short-term raw retention for a single tenant. :white_check_mark:
